https://enrsi.stvr.sk/articles/news/4545.text: President Peter Pellegrini left for China on Sunday evening. The three-day state visit is taking place at the invitation of Chinese head of state Xi Jinping. Their talks will focus on the further development of Slovak-Chinese relations, economic cooperation and current international issues. Discussions with Chinese officials will also cover support for high value-added investment and the development of cooperation in science and research, industry, transport, logistics, agriculture and tourism. Pellegrini will also visit major technology centres, including, for example, Baidu, which is one of the world's leading companies in the fields of artificial intelligence, cloud technologies and autonomous mobility. On Friday (24 July), Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian stated that Slovakia is an important partner for China in Europe, and under the leadership of Chinese President Xi Jinping and Slovak leaders, the two countries are maintaining strong relations and achieving fruitful results in various areas. It's the fifth visit to be paid by a Slovak head of state to China since the founding of independent Slovakia and the first in 16 years. It will conclude 29 July. Source: TASR

https://nineoclock.ro/romania-opens-new-.text: ABOUT US NINE O’CLOCK STAFF 2024 COMMERCIAL OFFER – 2026 Subscribe to the Nine O’Clock 2026 CONTACT Special price offer 2026 with a 50% discount The first public museum, in which all the essential functions regarding the storage, conservation and exhibition of cultural heritage, built from scratch in Romania, were designed and implemented, opened on Sunday, August 30, 2026, in Floresti, near Cluj Napoca. MuTRA – The Historical Gallery of Transylvania, part of the National Museum of Transylvanian History, is a construction of 11,344 m 2 and takes place on a terrain of over 15,000 m 2 . The work required an investment of 145 million lei, of which 60% represent PNRR funds through an agreement signed with the Ministry of Investments and European Projects (MIPE), and 40% were covered by financing from the state budget, through the Ministry of Culture (MC). Felix Marcu, manager of MNIT, said that this is the first construction in the country conceived, designed and executed to serve in a coherent way the needs of preservation, research and restoration of museum collections, with the ultimate goal of making them accessible to the general public. Organized in a modern, large-scale museum center, facilities such as: exhibition spaces, museum deposits, conservation-restoration laboratories and scientific investigations on heritage, a multimedia room, museum pedagogy rooms, commercial and relaxation spaces, as well as offices for the current activity of the institution’s staff. An infrastructure specially designed for the outdoors, with a green area and circulating terraces, will allow the hosting of cultural and leisure events, screenings and historical reenactment festivals. The need and concept initiated almost ten years ago, took shape by signing the contract on March 7, 2025, when the Technical Project was started. The construction works were started in June, and by August 30, 2026, 97% of the project were completed – essential and necessary works for public use, and the completion of the auxiliary (non-essential) works will be carried out this year, by the end of September. The opening of this museum meant much more than an ordinary inauguration event. The fact that the construction works and the completion of the Technical Project were carried out in record time, that the objective is a national premiere, and that the edifice itself and the facilities it has were made at the international standards that any worker in museum-type institutions and any consumer of culture and art wants, made the Minister of Culture, András István Demeter , to state the following, in his inaugural address: “Those who will be listed, present or not, here, today, are the ones who believe that they will go down in history because of two things. One is that they have made the difference between hoping and believing. (…) I want to bow to the teams of architects, engineers, builders; in front of the local authorities, in front of the community of Floresti. All of you, each with your own contribution and all of you, through your common contribution, starting today, are part of history. You and we have achieved a miracle together. But the best news is that the true miracle; The greater miracle begins only now.” The importance that this project carries for Romania and for the community was also revealed by the local officials, present at the event: Mr. Bogdan Pivariu, the mayor of Floresti, Mr. Emil Boc, Mayor of Cluj, Mrs. Maria Forna, Prefect of Cluj County, Mr. Vákár István, vice-president of the Cluj County Council. https://www.politico.eu/article/french-r.text: PARIS — Looting and rioting across France over the weekend are threatening to reshape the contours of the French presidential race. Far-right frontrunner Marine Le Pen is seizing on the crisis to cast herself as the candidate of law and order, but there are risks for her too. Many voters see her as a highly divisive leader whose 2027 victory would only deepen the societal fault lines exposed by the riots. Far-left firebrand Jean-Luc Mélenchon, widely tipped to challenge Le Pen in the second round next year, is also treading carefully as rivals accuse him of encouraging the rage on the streets that has morphed into pillaging and arson. Advertisement Advertisement For the flailing centrists, there is now an opportunity to finally make an impression in the contest — but only if they can distance themselves from President Emmanuel Macron, who is seen as fluffing his response to the nationwide wave of vandalism. Overall, it’s pushing the election into uncharted waters. “If there’s a real crisis, you don’t know where it could lead,” said one conservative who holds regular talks with officials from the far-right National Rally and was granted anonymity to discuss the subject. Where does that leave the candidates? POLITICO takes a look at the strategic calculus for the leading runners across the political spectrum. Marine Le Pen, on the up Le Pen is receiving an immediate boost. Even her rivals admit it. This Saturday’s unrest “benefits the far right,” said center-right European Member of Parliament Nathalie Loiseau. “They are circling around the violence like vultures,” she said in an interview. Advertisement Advertisement Le Pen has already cast herself as the alternative president, delivering a sober address to the nation Sunday and pitching herself as the candidate of a “ pacified France .” Jordan Bardella, president of her National Rally party, upped the ante on the protests and pitched his party as the only one able to restore order, dialing up fears about the pillaging. The rioters “will soon be breaking into people’s homes,” he said at a press conference in Paris. “The authorities are collapsing.” But excessive, prolonged chaos could backfire on a party long seen as instigating civil unrest. And the topic is already becoming a talking point inside the National Rally. Far-right party Rassemblement National candidate in France’s 2027 presidential election Marine Le Pen holds a press conference on the sidelines of a meeting of Patriots parliamentary group on the eve of an EU Summit in Brussels on October 14, 2026. | Nicolas Tucat/AFP via Getty Images “Some say that this shows that there will be riots if the National Rally comes to power,” said Charles-Henri Gallois, one of Bardella’s advisors. “But I don’t believe it.” According to the conservative quoted above, periods of instability can lead the French to turn their backs on anti-establishment figures and prefer traditional veterans. “You could end up with [Charles] De Gaulle on the Champs-Élysées,” the official said, referring to how the first president of the Fifth Republic emerged with extra powers after the 1958 crisis that roiled the nation. Advertisement Advertisement Jean-Luc Mélenchon , on the defensive Far-left leader Mélenchon is in a bind as he walks a tightrope between supporting protesters and distancing himself from violence. The France Unbowed party supported the school protests in the run-up to last weekend’s riots, and far-left elected officials have played a prominent role in the blockades, either in decrying alleged police violence or in support of the protesters. In the battle for leadership between Mélenchon and center-left MEP Raphaël Glucksmann, the former grabbed the limelight. Jean-Luc Melenchon, during the October 17 demonstration in Paris on October 17, 2026. | Augustin Pasquini/Hans Lucas/AFP via Getty Images But the violence this weekend could end up marginalizing the far left, especially with the government and political rivals accusing them of fueling the unrest. “They tried to aggravate the situation,” Loiseau said. According to a poll from Cluster 17 for POLITICO, the 75-year-old far-left firebrand is already one of the most commonly “rejected” politicians in France. On Monday, Mélenchon tried to turn the tables, firing back at the government, saying the prime minister was fomenting “disorder” with his accusations that ultra-left groups were trying to disrupt the election. Advertisement Advertisement Edouard Philippe, looking for a reset For the center-right presidential hopeful Philippe, the riots aren’t good news either. He has to work hard to distance himself from his old boss, President Emmanuel Macron, who is seen as failing to respond sufficiently to the crisis. (Philippe was Macron’s first prime minister.) But the protests could also be his opportunity to show some character, and rebut critics who think his campaign lacks energy and panache . Philippe, the best-placed centrist candidate to beat the far-right, has seen his poll ratings stall in recent months and has struggled to cut through the campaign noise. Edouard Philippe gives a speech during a meeting between the Alliance for General News Press and several presidential candidates in Paris on October 14, 2026. | Dimitar Dilkoff/AFP via Getty Images A break with Macron might just be what he needs. Philippe came out hard against the president after he failed to announce any measures during his primetime television address Sunday. “I would have preferred… decisions and initiatives to restore order,” he wrote online. “This country needs someone in command.” But the former PM will need to stick his neck out more if he’s going to make an impact. “He’s very presidential, and it’s a posture that suits him,” said one of Macron’s ministers, who, like others cited here, was granted anonymity to speak candidly. Advertisement Advertisement “But he’s not saying anything. What’s his measure? Why doesn’t he say we need to call a state of emergency? “ Raphaël Glucksmann, on the offensive For the MEP Raphaël Glucksmann, the protests are a trial by fire after he won the Socialist Party primary contest earlier this month and became the center-left’s presidential candidate. On Monday, Glucksmann tried to strike a very different note from Mélenchon, telling reporters that “it’s unbearable … that hordes of looters should attack symbols of the state.” Raphaël Glucksmann, Member of the European Parliament, co-chair of Place publique, and winner of the left-wing primary for the 2027 presidential election, speaking after his victory during the first-round results night at the Solaris in Paris on October 11, 2026. | Benjamin Vodant/Hans Lucas/AFP via Getty Images Sensing a chink in the far-left leader’s armor, he accused the leader of France Unbowed of being “a springboard” for Le Pen, who would be “the beneficiary of the chaos.” Glucksmann has seen his poll ratings go up since he won the Socialist Party primary outright, reaching 15% to 16.5% according to a recent Elabe poll — in a similar territory to Mélenchon and Philippe. But the minister quoted above expected Glucksmann to peak soon. Advertisement “He can only take voters away from Mélenchon,” the minister said. “A left-wing voter may vote for the right, but a right-wing voter won’t vote for the left anytime soon,” the person said. Emmanuel Macron, on the skids Macron is being roasted for going on television to address the nation and announce … absolutely nothing. On Sunday, Macron promised that rioters who “destroyed” things would have to pay the price and called for “clear answers” on why the protests turned violent. “Fucking hell, it’s rubbish,” said one former senior government official. Macron has cultivated an image of being above the fray and went on a trip to the Middle East on Monday. But his failure to respond to the violence risks damaging his final months in power. “It’s out of touch,” a regional official said. According to the minister quoted above, Macron should have let his prime minister do the talking but instead was encouraged to make “a speech to calm” the situation. Advertisement On Monday, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu tried to get a grip on the situation, announcing localized curfews, movement restrictions, and bans on public demonstrations. But another day of demonstrations has already been announced for next Saturday, sparking fears the protests will snowball into sustained protests similar to the Yellow Vests movement in 2018 and 2019. If so, this chaos will be a defining element of the 2027 campaign.
